notes: Derived edit: the premises entail the original through the catalogued chain has_father o has_father ⊑ has_paternal_grandfather. 'A father / paternal grandfather is an ancestor' now come from the catalogue (has_father is the inverse of father_of ⊑ parent_of ⊑ ancestor_of; paternal_grandfather_of ⊑ grandparent_of ⊑ ancestor_of), so the local rules are gone (FINDINGS B2). The rule premise is definitional and is also read backward as the firm rule pgf_def; the worlds add no answer: w1 only gives up the father's father, w2 gives up the child's father and adds an unnamed other father (placeholder, so the rule can fire) (FINDINGS E, re-encoded 2026-10-31). q1's 'no' before the edit rests on the record's bridge 'No member of the Darwin family was an ancestor of Aage Bohr' (no_darwin), which the edit contradicts, so every world gives it up (top-level gives_up), as the worlds' assumes say. This replaces the unstated firm rule 'darwin_only_via_george' (FINDINGS C2). q3 compares two people's fathers (fol).

queries.not_checked: fol: compares the fathers of two people (full brothers)

fol.notes: People are an uninterpreted sort; has_father is a function (the catalogued relation is functional) and so is has_mother (local), so 'the same father' and 'the same mother' are equalities of terms; the definitions are instantiated for the individuals asked about (Aage; Niels and Harald), which keeps Z3 quantifier-free and the 'no' needs only that George Darwin and Christian Bohr are different people (firm). has_paternal_grandfather is a function too, tied to the father's father by the firm definitional premise (the DL file's pgf_def). The worlds give up the premise the DL file gives up (w1 Niels's father, w2 Aage's father); w2's other father needs no placeholder, since has_father is total. The Darwin-ancestor side fact (no_darwin) plays no part in q3 and is left out. The shared mother is the chain's 'same mother' step, firm (w1's assumes keep Ellen Adler as both brothers' mother).

local.has_mother: has_mother(p): person p's mother (one per person); the catalogue has only mother_of, many-valued from the mother's side

No arithmetic, as the grammar 'same branch' queries.
